newsitem.title: USA: Compaq says new handheld computer a hot seller.
newsitem.headline: Compaq says new handheld computer a hot seller.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp. President Eckhard Pfeiffer said Tuesday he was "scrambling" to increase production of the company's new handheld computer because demand was much higher than expected.
The strong sales indicated that the time for the pocket-size computer may have at last arrived, he said.

Compaq's PC Companion, which supports many of the features of a desktop computer and weighs less than 1 pound, went on the market just two days ago. It uses a Microsoft Windows CE operating system and is thoroughly compatible with standard PCs so they can communicate back and forth.

"Response to the product is very strong. We had planned a certain volume and we're scrambling to pick up the volume because demand is stronger than anticipated," he told reporters after a ceremony at Compaq headquarters marking the sale of the company's one millionth server, or network computer.

Pfeiffer said the PC Companion, which sells for between $499 and $699, was proving to be a popular item for people shoping for Christmas presents. "That's why we wish we had a few more of them," he said.

The PC Companion's success stands in sharp contrast to the dismal failure that was the Apple Newton, the first of the pocket computers when it came out several years ago. Despite a heavy promotional campaign by Apple, the early Newtons proved to be a bust.
"The Newton was too little, too soon and really left the customer disappointed," Pfeiffer said. "The expectation was so much higher than the reality could be."

Now, he said, people understand the limitations inherent in pocket computers, such as screen size and the inability to do true word processing. "People do not expect a lot more than it can deliver," he said.
"I think the market is ready for the product," Pfeiffer said. "We think we're coming in at the right time."

Pfeiffer said the PC Companion's sales were part of an overall "seasonal uptick" as consumers start their holiday shopping. Historically, he said, "consumer and commercial (sales) have their peak in the fourth quarter and that is going to be the case again in 1996."
He said Compaq sees continued strong demand for PCs next year, with the overall market growing around 20 percent.

So optimistic is Compaq about the future that Pfeiffer said the company's internal projections show it reaching $40 billion in annual revenues by the end of this decade. Last year, Compaq had $14.8 billion in revenues.
